Applying to Tamatem Games

I grew up playing Tamatem games. Now I want to help build them.

I’m Batool, a Digital Business student at Al-Quds University. I’m applying to the Tamatem Internship Program in Amman, and I’d like to stay for my next five training periods.

Meet me in ten seconds

A game-style intro to my journey: each placement is a level, and my skills are the stats.

Why Tamatem

Fashion Queen was one of my games. It was also the first game aimed at women players in Arabic, and Tamatem brought it here.

That is what I admire: you give young people the space and the tools to grow and be creative. I want to learn how that works from the inside.

How I work

Team first. One of my greatest strengths is my ability to communicate effectively, build strong relationships, and support others in finding solutions to challenges.

I negotiate well. I listen, stay calm and bring people toward an idea I believe in.

Ideas under pressure. When a problem gets deep, a solution tends to click, and I follow it through.

My plan for five periods

The order is flexible. I’ll follow what Tamatem needs most. Tap a quest to see my first 30 days.

  1. 1. Community and player support

    Player feedback, community channels, escalations. I bring: staying steady with people.

    First 30 days: learn the player channels, answer feedback, and turn the top three complaints into a short report.

  2. 2. Marketing, social media and influencers

    Creatives, hooks, cross-promotion. I bring: audience psychology from Al-Balqa.

    First 30 days: study your best creatives, test three new hooks for the opening seconds, and report what held attention.

  3. 3. Business development and data

    Dashboards on retention and spend. I bring: the Python dashboard I built.

    First 30 days: build a simple dashboard of retention and spend, and flag one trend worth acting on.

  4. 4. The team that is mine (periods 4 and 5)

    Lead a project from start to finish, turning ideas into actionable solutions and building on a university-developed prototype to drive further development and innovation.

    First 30 days: agree one project with my mentor and ship a first version.

Dual studies in one minute

My degree alternates three months at the university with three months inside a company, over four years: eight training periods, and I’ve done three. Al-Quds launched it in 2015 on the German model, calls it the first of its kind in the Arab world, and works with more than 200 partner companies in Palestine.

A company gets a trainee who comes back for several periods and learns the business from inside.
